name: Gram Anubhav
line: Four to five days in rural Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat or Himachal.
deck: Purely experiential, which here means you are not shown a village. You stay in one, eat in one, and do a day's work in one.

figures.label: Grassroots partners in the villages themselves

aims.p: The objective is a few days of ordinary life instead of a circuit of one. What makes the difference is arriving as a guest and not as an audience.

aims.h: Hand the week to the host
aims.p: The people whose community this is set the four days. Our job stops at getting a school group there and staying out of the way of it.

aims.h: Put the work at the centre
aims.p: Shramdaan is the part we will not cut. A day spent doing the work is a different thing from a day spent being told about it.

how.p: Over a hundred grassroots organisations and social movements host these journeys in their own communities. We arrive with a school group. They decide what the group is shown.

how.h: Four states, four different water problems
how.p: Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh. A hill village's water problem and a desert village's water problem are not the same problem, and four days is long enough to stop treating them as one.

how.h: Nobody comes back with a project
how.p: There is no deliverable at the end of it. That is deliberate, and it is the hardest part to sell to a school: the journey is the exposure, and what a fifteen-year-old does with it is theirs.

activities.name: Shramdaan
activities.p: A day of physical work beside people who do it every day. It is the part nobody expects and the part everybody remembers.

activities.name: Village interactions
activities.p: Time with the people whose community this is, on their terms and at their pace. The host organisation decides what that looks like.

activities.name: Home visits
activities.p: Inside a house, at a hearth, eating what the household eats. The smallest room on the journey and the one that changes the most minds.

activities.name: Cultural evenings
activities.p: Run by the village rather than for it. That distinction is the whole difference between a journey and a package.

who.p: A cohort travels together for four or five days. The group arrives already knowing each other, which is what makes the evenings work.
The journey happens in somebody's community and is run by the organisations inside it. It is their programme as much as ours, and they are the reason it is not a tour.

who.h: Students who have only read about it
who.p: Water scarcity is a chapter until you carry some. A few days in one village is the shortest way out of the abstraction.

done.p: Over sixty Gram Anubhavs organised, run with over a hundred grassroots partners in the villages themselves.

holes.what: Twelve frames were filed under this journey and not one of them is a photograph of it — they carry page borders, hands that merge into the tools they are holding, and captions naming states this journey does not go to.
holes.unlocks: One real frame from one real Gram Anubhav. Sixty of these have been run, so the photographs exist somewhere; what is on file here is not them.

holes.what: More than a hundred grassroots organisations host these journeys and not one of them is named on this page.
holes.unlocks: Five host organisations named, with permission, would turn a count into a list of collaborators — and it is their programme as much as ours.

holes.what: No start year is published for the programme, so sixty journeys is a total and not a rate.

invite.note: The hosts are the hard part of this and they are already in place; what a journey needs is a school willing to give up five days.
